metric_identity.metric_name: AI Training Data & Synthetic Data Market
metric_identity.source_report: Grand View Research 'AI Training Dataset Market Size, Share | Industry Report 2033' (primary for training data), Research Nester / IndustryARC 'Synthetic Data Generation Market' (primary for synthetic data), supplemented by Fortune Business Insights, MarketsandMarkets, Epoch AI ('Will we run out of data to train large language models?'), and Gartner synthetic data predictions
metric_identity.publication_date: 2025 (Grand View Research updated report); December 2025 (Epoch AI blog update); July 2021 / June 2022 (Gartner synthetic data predictions)
metric_identity.methodology_notes: Grand View Research uses a combination of secondary research (industry publications, annual reports, regulatory databases) and primary research (interviews with industry experts, key opinion leaders, and C-level executives). Market is segmented by type (text, image/video, audio), by vertical (IT, automotive, healthcare, BFSI, retail), and by region. Market size is based on revenue generated by data providers, labeling platforms, and annotation tools. Synthetic data market sizing by Research Nester and IndustryARC covers revenue from synthetic data generation platforms and services, including tabular, image, text, and time-series synthetic data. Epoch AI's data wall analysis uses a bottom-up inventory of publicly available text data stocks, estimated at ~300 trillion quality-adjusted tokens, combined with current training scaling trends.

metric_value.value: AI Training Dataset Market: $3.195B (2025), projected $16.32B by 2033. Synthetic Data Market: $447M (2025), projected $8.79B by 2035. Alternate estimates: Fortune Business Insights values training data at $3.59B (2025) growing to $23.18B by 2034; MarketsandMarkets projects $9.58B by 2029 for training datasets; synthetic tabular data alone valued at $1.88B (2025) growing to $6.73B by 2029. Available human-generated training data stock: ~300 trillion quality-adjusted tokens (Epoch AI).
metric_value.geographic_scope: Global (North America dominates with 35.1% share in training data market)
metric_value.comparison_baseline: Training data market grew from ~$2.6B (2024 estimated) to $3.195B (2025). Synthetic data grew from negligible market share in 2020 to $447M in 2025. Gartner predicted 60% of AI training data would be synthetic by 2024 (from 1% in 2021). Image/video datasets dominate at 41.9% of training data market in 2025. Data labeling and annotation software held the largest market share in the training dataset value chain in 2024.

trend.year_over_year_change: Training data market: ~23% YoY growth from 2024 to 2025. Synthetic data market: ~31% YoY growth (from ~$341M in 2024 to $447M in 2025). Synthetic tabular data specifically growing at 37.9% YoY. The synthetic data segment is the fastest-growing sub-category within AI training data, projected at 30.5-37.9% CAGR depending on sub-segment.
trend.compound_annual_growth_rate: AI Training Dataset Market: 22.6% CAGR (2026-2033) per Grand View Research; 22.9% CAGR per Fortune Business Insights. Synthetic Data Market: 34.7% CAGR per Research Nester; 32% CAGR per IndustryARC (reaching $2.5B by 2030); 39.4% CAGR per Mordor Intelligence (reaching $2.67B by 2030). Synthetic tabular data: 37.6-37.9% CAGR.
trend.forecast_value: Training Data: $16.32B by 2033 (Grand View Research); $23.18B by 2034 (Fortune Business Insights); $9.58B by 2029 (MarketsandMarkets). Synthetic Data: $8.79B by 2035 (Research Nester); $2.5B by 2030 (IndustryARC); $2.67B by 2030 (Mordor Intelligence). Gartner predicts synthetic data will 'completely overshadow real data in AI models' by 2030.
trend.velocity_indicator: Data wall timeline: human-generated public text data exhausted between 2026 and 2032 (Epoch AI), with high-quality language data potentially depleted as early as 2026 under aggressive overtraining scenarios. Synthetic data adoption doubling time: from 1% of AI data in 2021 to 60%+ predicted by 2024 (Gartner). NVIDIA acquired Gretel Labs for $320M in March 2025, signaling infrastructure-layer investment in synthetic data. Cost halving time for data generation is accelerating as generative AI improves synthetic data quality.

entrepreneurial_relevance.relevance_for_entrepreneurs: This metric captures two converging forces that reshape the AI startup landscape. First, the $3.2B training data market growing at 22.6% CAGR represents the foundational 'picks and shovels' layer of AI — every model needs data, and the cost and complexity of acquiring quality training data is a persistent bottleneck. For startup founders, this means: (1) The 'data wall' is real and imminent — Epoch AI estimates high-quality text data could be exhausted as early as 2026. This creates massive opportunity for companies that can generate, curate, or augment training data. (2) Synthetic data ($447M in 2025, growing 34.7% CAGR) is the fastest-growing segment and represents a genuine paradigm shift. Gartner predicted 60% of AI data would be synthetic by 2024, and the trend is accelerating. Startups building synthetic data pipelines have a structural tailwind. (3) NVIDIA's $320M acquisition of Gretel Labs (March 2025) validates the synthetic data thesis at the infrastructure level — the GPU giant sees data generation as integral to its AI ecosystem. (4) Privacy regulations (GDPR, EU AI Act) are a major driver: synthetic data lets companies train models without exposing real personal data, creating compliance-driven demand especially in healthcare, finance, and European markets. (5) The image/video segment (41.9% of market) and multimodal datasets are the fastest-growing data types, driven by computer vision, autonomous vehicles, and multimodal AI models. (6) Data labeling and annotation remain labor-intensive despite automation — companies like Scale AI have built billion-dollar businesses on this pain point, and the market is far from saturated. (7) For non-data-focused AI startups: training data costs are a significant line item, and the shift to synthetic data could reduce data acquisition costs by 50-80%, materially improving unit economics.
entrepreneurial_relevance.actionable_insight: Consider building with synthetic data augmentation from day one — it reduces data acquisition costs, addresses privacy compliance (critical for EU/French market), and provides unlimited training data for niche use cases. For vertical AI startups, proprietary data moats remain the strongest competitive advantage; focus on collecting domain-specific data that cannot be easily synthesized. Monitor the data wall timeline: if high-quality text data runs out by 2026-2028, companies with proprietary datasets or superior synthetic data capabilities will have a structural advantage over competitors relying on public data.

confidence.cross_reference: Training data market size is corroborated across multiple analyst firms: Grand View Research ($3.195B in 2025), Fortune Business Insights ($3.59B in 2025), MarketsandMarkets (projected $9.58B by 2029), Business Research Insights ($7.48B by 2026 — notably higher, possibly using broader scope). The ~22-23% CAGR range is consistent across Grand View Research and Fortune Business Insights. Synthetic data market estimates show wider variance: Research Nester ($447M/2025), Mordor Intelligence ($510M/2025), IndustryARC (reaching $2.5B by 2030). Epoch AI's data wall analysis is widely cited by PBS, World Economic Forum, Berkeley, and multiple AI research outlets. Gartner's 2021 prediction (60% synthetic by 2024) is a specific, dated forecast that can be partially validated.
confidence.caveats: Training data market definitions vary significantly across analyst firms, leading to 2-3x variance in sizing (Grand View at $3.2B vs Business Research Insights at $7.5B for similar years). Some estimates include data labeling/annotation services, while others focus purely on dataset sales. Synthetic data market is nascent and definition boundaries are blurry — some reports count internal synthetic data generation (e.g., at Google or OpenAI) while others only count commercial synthetic data platforms. Gartner's 2021 prediction that 60% of AI data would be synthetic by 2024 is difficult to verify empirically and may have been overly aggressive. The Epoch AI data wall estimate (2026-2032) depends heavily on assumptions about overtraining ratios and data reuse, which are evolving rapidly. NVIDIA's acquisition of Gretel at $320M was not independently confirmed by all sources. The synthetic data CAGR estimates (32-39.4%) suggest high uncertainty about market trajectory.
